library(dplyr)

For this project, I will be working with 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024 data from the Public Use Microdata Sample (PUMS) Census API. First, I obtained an api key from the Census API website.

key <- "6ba7e209537814e77a7b7fc5aa8df5552ef8591b"

Sample API call:

pums2024 <- GET(paste0("https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs1/pums?get=SEX,PWGTP,MAR&SCHL=24&key=", key))


Part 1: Data Processing

Parsing Variable Values
Get 2021 variables:

vars2021 <- GET("https://api.census.gov/data/2021/acs/acs1/pums/variables.json")

vars2021 <- fromJSON(rawToChar(vars2021$content))

vars2021 <- list(
  AGEP = vars2021$variables$AGEP$values,
  GASP = vars2021$variables$GASP$values,
  GRPIP = vars2021$variables$GRPIP$values,
  JWAP = vars2021$variables$JWAP$values,
  JWDP = vars2021$variables$JWDP$values,
  JWMNP = vars2021$variables$JWMNP$values,
  PWGTP = vars2021$variables$PWGTP$values,
  FER = vars2021$variables$FER$values,
  HHL = vars2021$variables$HHL$values,
  SCH = vars2021$variables$SCH$values,
  SCHL = vars2021$variables$SCHL$values,
  SEX = vars2021$variables$SEX$values,
  ST = vars2021$variables$ST$values,
  REGION = vars2021$variables$REGION$values,
  DIVISION = vars2021$variables$DIVISION$values
  )
